pages.text: A black hole has entropy $(thing)S = Ac³/(4Għ)$() - its area in Planck units over four - the most any region can hold: the $(item)Bekenstein Crystal$(). It evaporates; if what comes out is purely thermal, what fell in is gone, and quantum mechanics forbids that.

The $(item)Page Curve Analyzer$() follows Hawking quanta through an evaporation. Firewalls and soft hair are two answers. The third: the radiation's entropy rises, then after the $(thing)Page time$() - when half the hole's entropy is gone, at M/√2 - falls back to zero. A $(item)Page Curve Record$() carried in the off hand keeps your hotbar in order (no Information Loss). With an ER bridge, it finds the $(item)Island$() that makes the curve turn.
